description: Executor.validate() MUST NOT disclose module-level introspection to a caller the ACL denied (PROTOCOL_SPEC §12.8.5.1). preflight() and preview() are module-authored code whose output names what a call would do — the resolved binary and argv of a command-wrapping module, the target of a write. Module lookup (Step 3) precedes the ACL check (Step 4), so guarding these hooks on 'lookup succeeded' alone runs them for a denied caller and returns what they say. All three SDKs did exactly that until spec v1.13.0. The rule is about AUTHORIZATION, not validity: a failed schema check does not suppress introspection, because a caller the ACL permits is entitled to hear what the module would do even when its inputs are malformed.

driver_contract.path: MUST drive the real Executor.validate() against a real Registry and a real ACL — not a hand-assembled PreflightResult. The defect this fixture pins lives in validate()'s own gating, so a driver that constructs the result itself asserts nothing.
driver_contract.module: The driver MUST register a module matching `module_contract` below: `preflight()` returns exactly the one warning string in `preflight_returns`, and `preview()` returns exactly one Change equal to `preview_change`. Both carry `sentinel` verbatim.
driver_contract.sentinel: `sentinel` is a disclosure canary. It appears in no value the Executor computes on its own, so finding it anywhere in the serialized PreflightResult proves module-level introspection ran and reached the caller. Cases carrying `expected.sentinel_absent` MUST serialize the WHOLE result (checks, warnings, errors, predicted_changes) and assert the substring is absent.
driver_contract.hooks_invoked: MUST be observed by recording invocations inside the module's own preflight()/preview() bodies. Asserting only on the absent check entries is weaker: an implementation that calls the hooks and then drops their results still ran module code for a denied caller, which is the side-effect half of the requirement.
driver_contract.checks_absent: MUST assert the named check is not present in `checks` AT ALL. A present-but-empty `module_preflight` entry does not satisfy it — the presence of the entry is itself the disclosure that the module implements the hook.
driver_contract.checks_present: A SUBSET assertion: each named check MUST appear in `checks`. The full list varies with the SDK's execution strategy (context / call_chain / module_lookup / approval entries) and is deliberately not pinned here.
driver_contract.failed_checks: The EXACT set of checks whose `passed` is false, order-insensitive. Exactness matters: `acl` alone is what a denied caller may learn, and a driver asserting only 'acl is among the failures' would not notice a second failure carrying module detail.

test_cases.description: The headline rule. A denied caller learns that it was denied and nothing else the module would have said.
The control. Without it, an implementation that never runs the hooks at all also passes the case above.

The rule is scoped to authorization. `confirm` is required and missing, so the schema check fails — and the permitted caller still gets the module's account of what would happen, which is what it needs in order to fix the call. `acl` is deliberately not asserted present here: SDKs differ on whether the checks that passed before a raising step survive in the list, which is a separate question from this one.
Denial wins over every other outcome. An implementation that ordered the two rules the other way round — introspect unless the schema failed — would pass the first case by accident and leak here.
